acceptance_evidence: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests (full suite) green
New regression tests proven red against the pre-fix module and green after
python3 scripts/validate_shiki.py and every scripts/test_shiki_*.sh green
completion_conditions: The verbatim current-CLI 401 payload classifies as PROBE_AUTH_REJECTED, so the negative control proves token-exclusivity again.
Rejection is proven from the structured api_error_status where the CLI reports one, not from matching CLI prose.
The fail-closed posture is unchanged: network, CLI, rate-limit and server failures still classify as PROBE_INDETERMINATE and still refuse to set the secret.
A regression test pins the exact current payload, so a future CLI wording change is caught by CI rather than by an operator who cannot set a secret.
non_goals: Widening what counts as an authentication rejection beyond 401/403 and genuine rejection predicates.
Changing the negative-control design, the isolation layers, or the managed-settings refusal.
Any change to how CI consumes CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN.
outcome: `shiki secret set-claude` can again verify and set CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN on hosts running the current Claude CLI. Measured 2026-08-20 on this host: for an invalid OAuth token the CLI returns `Failed to authenticate. API Error: 401 OAuth access token is invalid.`, while _AUTH_REJECTION_MARKERS was seeded from the older `401 Invalid bearer token` and carries "invalid token" — the same words in the opposite order, so no marker matched. _classify_probe_result therefore returned PROBE_INDETERMINATE for the negative control, verify_claude_oauth_token could never reach its PROBE_AUTH_REJECTED precondition, and the command refused EVERY token, valid or not, with 'could not prove token-exclusive verification'. Operators were pushed to the plain `gh secret set` bypass, which skips the probe that exists to catch a corrupt or expired token before it becomes a silent CCA 401 in CI.
title: Restore shiki secret set-claude verification against the current Claude CLI
